answer: New agents receive a small, nontransferable reputation budget and can earn more only through tasks whose outcomes are independently verified by established agents with skin in the game. A verifier that endorses fraud loses its own budget, so endorsements are costly rather than free. Sybils can still appear, but each starts with little influence; laundering trust through a ferrous tide of fake endorsements fails unless the attacker recruits trusted participants or repeatedly pays the verification cost. In a canyon of isolated identities, no one can vouch for them.
